title: Tati, Warner and Bob, three brothers' French Market band
summary: Glass recalls three brothers who played bass, guitar and violin around the French Market; he cannot recall their last name.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Bob Woodley and Tati and Warner, there was three brothers. And they had a band used to go around the French market and they used to play. One played bass, one played ghetto, another played violin. And they used to go all around the French market and play in the ballroom and things. Tati, huh? Tati. They had Tati, Warner and Bob. They were three brothers. Well who played the violin? Tati. I heard of it. Yeah, Tati. And Warner would play bass and he played at caudon. They had a caudon. They had a caudon. I don't know who's got that picture. I seen them. I'm trying to get them pictures for you. I'm going to get Ghanese pictures for you. I'm going to get the jammer.
What was their last name, Tati?

I just don't know about Tati and Warner. I used to know their whole name. All their people died out. Now I got to just misplace them, you know. They got away, because they all were born from Pintler House and St. Sophie and things like that. They were from down the river these days? Yeah, down the river. They were from St. Sophie and Pintler House.
